papers.title_in_file: Hamiltonian and Liouvillian learning in weakly-dissipative quantum many-body systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Theory and numerical study of learning the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators of an analog quantum simulator from quench data.

assertions.value: The authors report that the learning error first decreases with the inverse square root of the number of runs and later remains constant, which lets them recognize missing ansatz terms.
quotes: Initially, the learning error decreases with the inverse square root of the number of runs
Eventually the learning error remains constant, allowing us to recognize missing ansatz terms
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical study on two spin models; an empirical result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their method applies where dissipation is weak compared to the coherent evolution, and to a scenario with direct access to the quantum device.
quotes: Our method is applicable in a regime of experimental relevance where the dissipation is weak compared to the coherent evolution.
Our work applies to a scenario where one has direct access to the quantum device
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Section IV, p.11-12.

assertions.value: The authors report that randomized measurements allowed them to numerically demonstrate Hamiltonian learning for large systems of tens of spins.
quotes: this allowed us to numerically demonstrate Hamiltonian learning for large systems consisting of tens of spins
assertions.certainty_reason: A numerical (simulated) demonstration in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Simulation only, not an experiment on hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Direct implementation of a perceptron in superconducting circuit quantum hardware
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Hardware demonstration of an adiabatic controlled gate on superconducting qubits that acts as a perceptron building block of a quantum neural network.

assertions.value: The authors report a superconducting qubit implementation of an adiabatic controlled gate that generalizes the action of a classical perceptron as the basic building block of a quantum neural network.
quotes: we demonstrate a superconducting qubit implementation of an adiabatic controlled gate, which generalizes the action of a classical perceptron as the basic building block of a quantum neural network.
assertions.certainty_reason: One hardware experiment reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that the time to run the equivalent gate-decomposed circuit scales exponentially in the number of qubits.
quotes: In contrast, the time to run the equivalent circuit scales exponentially in the number of qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper argues this from gate-count estimates in Appendix A, not from a measured comparison.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison rests on estimated gate counts and fidelities.

assertions.value: The authors state that evaluating quantum advantage in larger networks is left to forthcoming investigations, and that limits on couplers per qubit or compromises in connectivity may reduce the stated advantage.
quotes: While we have demonstrated the entangling power of the perceptron gate, evaluating quantum advantage in larger networks is subject to forthcoming investigations.
Limitations imposed by the number of couplers that can be physically attached to a single qubit or compromises in the connectivity between layers may reduce this advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limits in Section IV, p.6-7.

papers.title_in_file: Robustness of Variational Quantum Algorithms against stochastic parameter perturbation
papers.version_note: File carries the arXiv v3 title; same arXiv id 2301.00048 as the file name, whose title is the earlier 'On the gate-error robustness of variational quantum algorithms'.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Perturbative analysis plus simulations of how stochastic gate-parameter errors raise the energy of optimized variational circuits (VQE and QAOA).

assertions.value: The authors report that the change in energy due to gate errors behaves quadratically with respect to the spread of parameter deviations, which is equivalent to linear dependence on the gate error probabilities.
quotes: behaves quadratically with respect to the spread of parameter deviations, which is equivalent to linear dependence on the gate error probabilities
assertions.certainty_reason: Perturbative analysis confirmed by numerics; the paper does not state a theorem.

assertions.value: The authors state that they assess their findings against VQE and QAOA for various problems with up to 14 qubits, operating the circuits at their noiseless optimal parameters.
quotes: We assess our findings against the variational quantum eigensolver and quantum approximate optimization algorithm for various problems with up to 14 qubits.
impact the performance of variational algorithms when operated at their noiseless optimal parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the abstract and Section I.

assertions.value: The authors state that their study focused on energy perturbations around the noiseless optimum, while in practice training occurs in the presence of noise.
quotes: Importantly, whereas our study primarily focused on energy perturbations around the noiseless optimum
in practice, one has to train the algorithm in the presence of noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in Section V, p.8.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Simulation study of classifying Iris, breast cancer and MNIST data with a single d-level system (qudit) using metric learning and data re-uploading.

assertions.value: The authors report favorable comparisons against the best classical models for small qudits (dimension d < 5, L = 1, 2 layers) when feature dimension and class count are not much larger than the qudit dimension.
quotes: our results show favorable comparisons against the best classical models
This trend holds true even for small quantum systems, with dimensions d < 5 and utilizing algorithms with a few layers (L = 1, 2).
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated results on three datasets from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that for high-dimensional data such as MNIST, with a convolutional network reducing dimension, small quantum systems often act as bottlenecks and give lower accuracy than their classical counterparts.
quotes: we observe that small quantum systems often act as bottlenecks, resulting in lower accuracy compared to their classical counterparts
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that all simulations use full access to the wave function, and that their primary goal is not to claim superiority over other systems.
assertions.anchor: Sections I and III, p.2 and p.6
quotes: In all the simulations that will be presented throughout the manuscript, full access to the wave function of the system is available at all times.
without necessarily claiming any superiority over other systems
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup and goal in Sections I and III.

papers.title_in_file: Faster variational quantum algorithms with quantum kernel-based surrogate models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Numerical study of Gaussian-process surrogate models with classically evaluated quantum kernels for optimizing VQE.

assertions.value: The authors report that their quantum kernel-based approach consistently achieves significantly higher accuracy than stochastic gradient descent while requiring less than an order of magnitude fewer quantum circuit executions.
quotes: our quantum kernel-based approach is found to consistently achieve significantly higher accuracy while requiring less than an order of magnitude fewer quantum circuit executions
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulations from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The phrase as printed is ambiguous; Section IV text says SPSA needed more than an order of magnitude more evaluations.

assertions.value: The authors state that the strategy targets small-to-intermediate scale VQAs on noisy near-term processors, focuses on VQE, and is demonstrated numerically.
quotes: We present a new optimization strategy for small-to-intermediate scale variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) on noisy near-term quantum processors
We focus on the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) algorithm and demonstrate numerically
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the kernels are impractical to evaluate on-device because of the number of kernel evaluations needed, and that classical evaluation for more qubits quickly becomes intractable.
quotes: it is impractical to evaluate these kernels on-device
classical evaluation of the quantum kernels for more qubits quickly becomes intractable
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limits in Section VII.

papers.title_in_file: A didactic approach to quantum machine learning with a single qubit
papers.version_note: File name carries the earlier title 'Fraud detection with a single-qubit quantum neural network'; the text is the same arXiv paper 2211.13191 (v2).
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Tutorial and benchmark of single-qubit data re-uploading classifiers, including a credit card fraud detection task compared with classical neural networks.

assertions.value: The authors report that the results of Table 5 suggest the optimal number of layers for the fraud problem is 2.
quotes: The results of Table 5 suggest that the optimal number of layers for this problem is 2.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper tests the single-qubit premise on a real-world task, fraud detection using credit card transaction data.
quotes: this paper focuses on implementing and testing the premise in a real-world task, in particular, fraud detection using credit card transaction data.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results are promising but should not be taken as a proof of advantage.
quotes: These results are promising, but should not be taken as a proof of advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in Section 5, p.23.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum generative adversarial learning in photonics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Experimental and simulated QGAN on a programmable silicon quantum photonic chip, studying noise and defects.

assertions.value: The authors report that QGANs can generate high-quality quantum data with a fidelity higher than 90%, and that this is the first experimental demonstration of the QGAN model in photonics.
quotes: Our results show that QGANs can generate high-quality quantum data with a fidelity higher than 90%
we experimentally demonstrate the QGAN model in photonics for the first time
assertions.certainty_reason: Experiment and simulation from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the 4-mode universal linear optical circuit on their chip comprises 15 programmable phase shifters.
quotes: the 4-mode universal linear optical circuit [29] in our chip comprises 15 programmable phase shifters
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own chip setup in the defects section.

assertions.value: The authors state that effects of complex noise and defects in future large-scale photonic circuits with more photons warrant further study.
quotes: The future large-scale quantum photonic circuits with more photons will face complex noise and defects, and their effects on QGANs warrant further study.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in the Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: A QUBO model of the RNA folding problem optimized by variational hybrid quantum annealing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results or main analysis, discussion/conclusion; appendices and supplement skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a physically motivated RNA folding QUBO and trains it and two existing QUBOs on a D-Wave hybrid solver with classical SPSA.

assertions.value: The authors state that the new model 3 does not demonstrate any advantage over models 1 and 2 with respect to the training and testing structures of this work.
quotes: This result indicates that with respect to the training and testing structures of this work, model 3 does not demonstrate any advantage versus models 1 and 2, representing existing RNA folding QUBO models.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on 40 test structures from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they restricted training to only 30 small structures (20 to 50 bases) and ran only one execution of each problem instance.
quotes: we had to restrict our training data set to only 30 small structures (from 20 to 50 bases)
we opted for a greedy approach in which only one execution of each problem instance was run, both in the training and testing phases of our methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limits in Section IV.C.

assertions.value: The authors claim that, to the best of their knowledge, this is the first experimental paper that demonstrates variational hybrid quantum annealing.
quotes: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental paper that demonstrates the implementation of variational hybrid quantum annealing.
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim by the authors; not verified here.
